title: Dixon & Coles 1997 — Modelling Association Football Scores and Inefficiencies in the Football Betting Market
file_name: Dixon & Coles 1997 — Modelling Association Football Scores and Inefficiencies in the Football Betting Market.pdf
universal_lens: Dixon & Coles 1997 constructs a hierarchical Poisson-GLM where match scores (X,Y) follow a τ-perturbed bivariate Poisson with team-specific attack α_i, defense β_j, home advantage γ, and dependence ρ. The log-linear structure λ_ij = α_i β_j γ, μ_ij = α_j β_i embeds multiplicative team strengths into Poisson rates. Time dynamics enter via exponential decay weighting w(t) = exp(-ξΔt) in the likelihood, making parameters stochastic processes. The τ-function τ(x,y;ρ) = 1 - λμρ (0,0), 1+λρ (0,1), 1+μρ (1,0), 1-ρ (1,1), 1 otherwise preserves Poisson marginals while inducing negative correlation for low scores. MLE solves ∇ℓ(θ)=0 with θ={α,β,γ,ρ,ξ}, yielding a generative model where P(score|θ) > P_bookmaker(score) defines the betting edge.
gsi_mapping: GSI Bayesian layer: The model defines a conjugate-exponential family where prior team strengths α_i,β_i ~ Gamma(a,b) update via Poisson likelihood with decay-weighted observations. The τ-perturbation breaks conjugacy but preserves marginal Poisson sufficiency. Conformal inference applies: for each match, compute nonconformity score α = |P_model(home win) - P_bookmaker(home win)|; prediction sets C_ε = {y: α_y ≤ quantile(α,1-ε)} guarantee marginal coverage 1-ε under exchangeability. The decay parameter ξ controls effective sample size, trading bias-variance in posterior concentration. Bookmaker odds imply implicit probabilities π_b = 1/odds normalized; the model's posterior predictive P(y|D_t) dominates π_b in KL divergence when ρ,ξ are well-calibrated.
gse_mapping: GSE state-transition layer: Team strength state s_i(t) = (α_i(t), β_i(t)) evolves as s_i(t+1) = s_i(t) + η_i(t) with η ~ N(0,Σ_ξ) where Σ_ξ ∝ (1-exp(-2ξ)). Match outcome is observation y_t ~ τ-Poisson(λ(s_home,s_away), μ(s_away,s_home)). The betting decision a_t ∈ {bet home, bet away, bet draw, no bet} maximizes E[log(1 + r_t)] where r_t = (1/π_b(y_t) - 1)𝟙{bet on y_t} - 𝟙{bet ≠ y_t}. The value function V(s) satisfies Bellman equation with transition kernel induced by ξ. Breakdown occurs when ξ → 0 (static teams, overfit) or ξ → ∞ (no memory, high variance); optimal ξ* balances regime-switching detection vs. estimation noise.

primitives.name: Independent Bivariate Poisson Score Generator
primitives.verbatim_quote: An exception to this is the model due to Maher (1982), that assumes independent Poisson distributions for the number of goals scored by each of the home and away teams, with means that are specific to each team's past performance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: X_{ij}: home goals (count, dimensionless); Y_{ij}: away goals (count, dimensionless); \alpha_i: team i attack strength (goals^{1/2}, dimensionless rate multiplier); \beta_j: team j defense weakness (goals^{1/2}, dimensionless rate multiplier); \gamma: home advantage multiplier (dimensionless, >1); \lambda_{ij}, \mu_{ij}: Poisson rate parameters (goals per match, dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Goals scored by each team are independent conditional on team strengths; team strengths are constant over the estimation window; home advantage multiplies home attack rate only; Poisson dispersion equals mean (equidispersion); matches are independent given parameters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails for low-scoring matches (0-0, 1-0, 0-1, 1-1) where empirical dependence deviates from independence (p.6); equidispersion violated if goal variance ≠ mean; static parameters ignore form fluctuations; cannot model cross-league cup matches without league-strength bridging.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Base likelihood for Bayesian updating of (α,β,γ) with Gamma priors. GSE: Emission distribution for HMM where hidden state = team strengths; observation = (X,Y). The log-linear rate structure makes sufficient statistics additive for conjugate updates.
layer2.telemetry: Deviance residuals vs. fitted values; Pearson χ²/df for overdispersion; marginal Poisson goodness-of-fit (p.5: 'near perfect fit to aggregated data')

primitives.name: Low-Score Dependence Perturbation (τ-function)
primitives.verbatim_quote: However, in attempting to derive a model which is not just a reasonable description of the data, but which also has the potential to provide better estimates of probabilities than the subjective estimates ascribed by bookmakers, we have had to modify and enhance this basic model structure.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \rho: dependence parameter (dimensionless, bounds: \max(-1/\lambda, -1/\mu) \le \rho \le \min(1/(\lambda\mu), 1)); \tau(x,y;\rho): perturbation factor (dimensionless, preserves marginal Poissons); \lambda,\mu: Poisson rates from bivariate_poisson_score_model (goals per match)
primitives.assumptions: Dependence only affects scores with x≤1, y≤1; marginal distributions remain exactly Poisson(λ) and Poisson(μ); ρ is constant across all matches and teams; perturbation is multiplicative on the independence kernel.
primitives.breakdown_regime: ρ bounds violated if |ρ| too large → negative probabilities; fails to capture dependence for scores >1 (e.g., 2-2); assumes same ρ for all match contexts (derby vs. non-derby); cannot model positive correlation for low scores (ρ>0 increases 0-0,1-1 but decreases 0-1,1-0).

layer2.mapping: GSI: Non-conjugate likelihood correction; posterior requires MCMC or Laplace approximation. GSE: Modifies emission probabilities for low-score states, changing the value of betting on draws/underdogs. The τ-kernel is a rank-4 update to the independent Poisson transition matrix.
layer2.telemetry: Likelihood ratio test: 2(ℓ_τ - ℓ_indep) ~ χ²_1; empirical vs. model probabilities for (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1) (Table 1, p.5); estimated ρ ≈ 0.13 (p.7) with SE

primitives.name: Time-Varying Team Strength with Exponential Forgetting
primitives.verbatim_quote: These modifications account for the fluctuating performance of individual teams and also enable the estimation of match outcomes for cup competitions in which teams from different leagues play one another.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \xi: decay rate (matches^{-1}, dimensionless per match); w(t;\xi): observation weight (dimensionless, ∈(0,1]); T: current match index (matches); t: historical match index (matches); \ell: weighted log-likelihood (nats); \theta: all parameters including time-varying α_i(t), β_i(t)
primitives.assumptions: Team strength evolves as a continuous-time Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process discretized to exponential weighting; decay rate ξ is common across all teams and leagues; matches are conditionally independent given current strengths; cup matches use same ξ with league-strength offsets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: ξ → 0: static model, overfits early-season noise, ignores form changes; ξ → ∞: only last match matters, extreme variance, ignores season-long ability; optimal ξ* depends on league competitiveness and schedule density; breaks if team strength has structural breaks (manager change, key injury) not captured by smooth decay.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Equivalent to Gaussian random walk prior on log(α), log(β) with precision ∝ ξ; posterior mode = weighted MLE. GSE: State transition covariance Σ_ξ = (1-e^{-2ξ})I for log-strengths; ξ controls exploration-exploitation in betting policy. The weighting kernel is the Green's function of the continuous-time Kalman filter.
layer2.telemetry: Profile likelihood for ξ; out-of-sample log-score vs. ξ; rolling window calibration of PIT histograms; effective sample size N_eff = (∑w)²/∑w²

primitives.name: Joint MLE for Attack, Defense, Home Advantage, Dependence, Decay
primitives.verbatim_quote: The technique is based on a Poisson regression model but is complicated by the data structure and the dynamic nature of teams' performances.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \theta = {\alpha_i, \beta_i}_{i=1}^N \cup \{\gamma, \rho, \xi\}: parameter vector (dimensionless); N: number of teams (count); \Theta: parameter space with identifiability constraint ∑_i \log \alpha_i = 0 or ∏_i \alpha_i = 1; \hat{\theta}: MLE (dimensionless); identifiability: scale invariance (α_i → cα_i, β_i → β_i/c) fixed by constraint
primitives.assumptions: Global optimum exists and is unique; likelihood is concave in log-parameters; numerical optimization converges (Newton-Raphson/Fisher scoring); standard errors from observed Fisher information; cup matches included with league-strength bridging parameters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Flat likelihood ridges if teams play few matches (newly promoted); separation if team always wins/loses by large margins; non-identifiability without constraint; local maxima if ξ,ρ poorly initialized; computational cost O(N³) for Hessian inversion.

layer2.mapping: GSI: MLE = MAP with flat priors; Laplace approximation gives Gaussian posterior N(θ̂, I(θ̂)⁻¹). GSE: θ̂_t is the sufficient statistic for betting policy at time t; the score function ∇ℓ(θ̂) = 0 defines the equilibrium condition for market efficiency. The Fisher information I(θ̂) quantifies parameter uncertainty for Kelly betting.
layer2.telemetry: Gradient norm ||∇ℓ|| at convergence; condition number of Hessian; bootstrap SE vs. asymptotic SE; likelihood ratio tests for nested models (ρ=0, ξ=0, γ=1)

primitives.name: Positive Expected Return Betting Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: In making bets the challenge then is to find 'good bets', in which the considered probability of occurrence is higher than the corresponding probability determined by the bookmakers' odds, so that there is a positive expected return.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Pr_{\text{model}}(y): model probability for outcome y ∈ {H,D,A} (dimensionless, ∑=1); \pi_{\text{book}}(y): bookmaker implied probability (dimensionless, ∑>1 due to overround); \text{odds}(y): decimal odds (currency/currency); \text{Stake}: bet size (currency); \text{Expected return}: \Pr_{\text{model}}(y)/\pi_{\text{book}}(y) - 1 (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Bookmaker odds are fixed ~1 week before match (p.2); model probabilities are calibrated (PIT uniform); bettor is risk-neutral or uses Kelly fraction; no betting limits or market impact; overround is distributed proportionally across outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model miscalibration → false edges; bookmaker limits/sharp action moves odds before bet placement; overround distribution unknown (favorite-longshot bias); correlation between model error and bookmaker error; non-stationarity in bookmaker efficiency.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Decision rule minimizes expected Brier score under model posterior; equivalent to thresholding conformal p-values. GSE: Policy π(θ) = argmax_a E[R(a,y)|θ]; the edge δ = Pr_model - π_book is the advantage state variable. Kelly stake = δ / (1 - π_book) maximizes asymptotic growth rate log W_T.
layer2.telemetry: ROI = (∑ returns) / (∑ stakes); yield = ROI - 1; Sharpe = mean(return)/std(return); hit rate vs. model probability calibration plot; Closing line value (CLV) vs. opening odds

reasoning_traces.think:
The Dixon-Coles model represents a watershed in sports analytics: it transforms football scoring from a descriptive Poisson process into a generative, time-aware, betting-calibrated engine. The mathematical architecture has five interlocking primitives. First, the bivariate Poisson score model (Primitive 1) establishes the base likelihood: goals X,Y are independent Poissons with log-linear rates λ=α_hβ_aγ, μ=α_aβ_h. This is a generalized linear model with log link, where attack α and defense β are team-specific multiplicative factors. The identifiability constraint ∏α_i=1 (or ∑logα_i=0) resolves the scale invariance α→cα, β→β/c. Second, the τ-dependence correction (Primitive 2) perturbs the independence kernel only for (x,y)∈{0,1}² via τ(x,y;ρ). This is a rank-4 update to the probability tensor that preserves Poisson marginals exactly—a crucial property because it means the sufficient statistics for α,β remain the total goals scored/conceded, keeping MLE computationally tractable. The bounds on ρ (max(-1/λ,-1/μ) ≤ ρ ≤ min(1/λμ,1)) ensure non-negative probabilities. Third, exponential decay (Primitive 3) introduces time dynamics: the weighted log-likelihood ∑w(t)log Pr with w(t)=exp(-ξ(T-t)) is mathematically equivalent to a Gaussian random walk prior on log-strengths with precision ξ, or a continuous-time Kalman filter with process noise ∝ξ. The decay rate ξ controls the effective memory: N_eff = (∑w)²/∑w² ≈ 1/(1-e^{-2ξ}) for large T. Fourth, joint MLE (Primitive 4) estimates all parameters simultaneously. The gradient equations are ∂ℓ/∂α_i = ∑_t w(t)[X_t/λ_t - 1]β_{opp}γ + [Y_t/μ_t - 1]β_{opp} = 0 (and symmetric for β), with additional equations for γ,ρ,ξ. The Hessian is block-sparse (team parameters only couple through matches), enabling efficient Newton-Raphson. Fifth, the betting criterion (Primitive 5) is a threshold rule: bet when model probability exceeds bookmaker implied probability. The Kelly-optimal stake is (Pr_model - π_book)/(1 - π_book), maximizing E[log wealth]. The model's positive return (p.2) proves the market is not semi-strong efficient: public historical data + Poisson-GLM + τ-correction + decay weighting yields calibrated probabilities that dominate bookmaker odds. The breakdown regimes are instructive: ρ bounds violation → negative probabilities; ξ→0 → static overfit; ξ→∞ → high-variance noise-chasing; bookmaker limits → strategy infeasibility. The retrocausal genealogy traces from Maher 1982 (independent Poisson) through Dixon-Coles 1997 (τ, decay) to Rue-Salvesen 2000 (Bayesian dynamic), Baio-Blangiardo 2010 (hierarchical), and modern Dixon-Coles implementations in Stan/PyMC with full posterior inference. The theory of mind: bookmakers set odds to balance flow, not to predict; they shade lines toward public favorites (favorite-longshot bias), creating systematic edges on draws and underdogs where τ-correction matters most. The model exploits this by being 'honest' about low-score dependence. Cross-layer veto: the τ-correction and decay weighting are collinear in their effect on low-score probabilities—both increase P(0-0) and P(1-1) relative to independence. If ξ is too large, recent form dominates and ρ becomes unidentifiable; if ξ too small, ρ absorbs form changes. The veto condition is that the profile likelihood for (ξ,ρ) must have a well-defined interior maximum, not a ridge. Empirically, Dixon-Coles found ξ≈0.0065 (half-life ~106 matches) and ρ≈0.13, with positive ROI 1995-96.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Maher 1982 (independent Poisson with team-specific rates) → Dixon & Coles 1997 (τ-dependence + exponential decay + MLE betting) → Rue & Salvesen 2000 (Bayesian dynamic with Gaussian random walk) → Baio & Blangiardo 2010 (hierarchical model with team covariates) → Egidi et al. 2018 (mixture models for overdispersion) → Modern Stan/PyMC implementations with full posterior predictive checking and conformal calibration.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Bookmakers act as market makers: they set opening odds to attract balanced action, then adjust to manage liability. Their implied probabilities π_book contain an overround (∑π_book > 1) and systematic biases: favorite-longshot bias (underestimate underdog probability), draw aversion (underestimate draw probability), and recency bias (overweight recent form). The Dixon-Coles model exploits these by: (1) τ-correction accurately captures draw/low-score probabilities where bookmakers err most; (2) exponential decay with optimized ξ balances recency vs. stability better than bookmaker heuristics; (3) cup competition modeling handles cross-league matches where bookmakers have less information. The bettor's edge exists because bookmakers optimize for flow balance, not probabilistic calibration.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity veto: The τ-dependence parameter ρ and decay rate ξ both affect low-score probabilities (0-0, 1-1). High ξ (short memory) increases recent-form volatility, mimicking positive ρ; low ξ (long memory) smooths form, mimicking negative ρ. The profile likelihood ℓ(ξ,ρ) must exhibit a unique interior maximum—if the Hessian ∇²ℓ has near-zero eigenvalues along the (ξ,ρ) ridge, parameters are unidentifiable and betting edges are spurious. Leakage veto: Cup matches use league-strength bridging parameters; if these are estimated from the same data used for betting evaluation, look-ahead bias contaminates ROI. The veto requires strict temporal separation: parameters estimated only on matches strictly before the betting date, with cup bridges fixed from prior league interactions only.
